# Results — Study 339 (Convertible-Bonds) on the real total-return tapes

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). One recipe — fit the convexity
of **CWB** (SPDR Bloomberg Convertible Securities ETF) versus **SPY**, then race CWB against
a **beta-matched SPY/AGG blend** (annual rebalance, 2 bps one-way on turnover) on the
**total-return** tapes. Sharpes are **excess-of-cash** (SHY, 1-3y Treasuries) so a part-bond
instrument and a part-bond blend race like-for-like. As-of **2026-05-31**; match the
fingerprints to confirm you hold the same tapes.*

## Data stamp

CWB lists **2009-04-16**, which bounds the joint window honestly.

| Series | Window | Rows | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|---|
| CWB (convertibles, total return) | 2009-04-16 → 2026-05-29 | 4,307 | `1ba5397da707` |
| SPY (stocks, total return) | 2009-04-16 → 2026-05-29 | 4,307 | `32ea3bc507fb` |
| AGG (aggregate bonds, total return) | 2009-04-16 → 2026-05-29 | 4,307 | `e27a0b52d246` |
| SHY (1-3y Treasuries, cash proxy) | 2009-04-16 → 2026-05-29 | 4,307 | `515f22fb975e` |

## Is the payoff convex? — the quadratic regression

`r_CWB = α + β·r_SPY + γ·max(r_SPY, 0)²`. Convexity ("equity upside, bond downside") needs
**γ > 0** with a robust *t* ≥ 2 — a payoff that bends *up*.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Linear beta β (to SPY) | 0.658 |
| Convexity coefficient γ | **−1.897** |
| HAC (Newey-West) *t* on γ | **−2.96** |
| Block-bootstrap γ 95% CI (circular, 21d, 2000 reps) | **[−3.484, −0.873]** — wholly below 0 |
| P(γ > 0) across resamples | **0%** |
| R² | 0.692 |

The bend has the **wrong sign and is significant**: CWB's payoff is slightly *concave*, not
convex. → Signal **NONE** (the convexity claim is rejected, not merely unconfirmed).
Robust across halves: γ = **−1.847** (*t* −1.56) in 2009–2015 and **−2.322** (*t* −3.40) in
2016–2026.

## Does it catch more of the rally than the fall? — capture asymmetry

| Quantity | Value |
|---|--:|
| Up-capture (vs SPY, on up days) | 0.664 |
| Down-capture (vs SPY, on down days) | 0.645 |
| Asymmetry (up − down) | **+0.019** |

Essentially symmetric — not the asymmetric "catch the rally, cushion the fall" payoff sold.

## Can a plain matched blend keep up? — the race (excess-of-cash Sharpe, 2 bps/rebal)

Matched weight `w_stock = 0.63` (= CWB's equity beta to SPY); bond leg AGG.

| Arm | CAGR | Vol | Sharpe (xs) | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| CWB (convertibles) | 12.0% | 13.1% | 0.817 | −32.1% |
| **Matched blend (63% SPY / 37% AGG)** | 11.0% | **10.9%** | **0.879** | **−22.0%** |
| 100% stocks (SPY) | **15.6%** | 17.2% | 0.838 | −33.7% |
| AGG (aggregate bonds) | 2.8% | 4.7% | 0.378 | — |

| Question | Answer |
|---|--:|
| CWB − blend excess Sharpe | **−0.062** (blend wins on the point estimate) |
| Block-bootstrap Sharpe-difference 95% CI (21d, 2000 reps) | **[−0.308, +0.185]** — straddles 0 |
| CWB wins the Sharpe race in … of resamples | **30%** |
| HAC *t* on the daily (CWB − blend) return difference | **+0.71** (not significant) |

The matched blend **edged** CWB on risk-adjusted return at a smaller drawdown, and the
difference is a statistical coin flip → CWB is, at best, indistinguishable from the cheap DIY
mix. → Tradability **MIRAGE**.

## The bond floor when it mattered — March 2020 (worst SPY month)

| Series | March 2020 return |
|---|--:|
| SPY (stocks) | −12.5% |
| **CWB (convertibles)** | **−13.1%** |
| Matched blend | −7.7% |
| AGG | −0.5% |

CWB fell **more than the stock market** in the crash — the advertised "bond floor" was not
there. → 3rd axis **"Equity upside, bond downside?" → BUSTED**.

## How to read it

- **No convexity.** The defining feature of a convertible — a payoff that bends up — is
  *absent* from the CWB tape; the fitted curvature is negative and significant. → Signal
  **NONE**.
- **A cheaper DIY blend matches it.** A 63/37 SPY/AGG mix beat CWB on Sharpe at a smaller
  drawdown, and you avoid CWB's ~0.40%/yr fee. → Tradability **MIRAGE**.
- **The floor failed in the crash.** CWB fell harder than SPY in March 2020 (HY-credit beta
  sells off *with* equities), so "bond downside" is **BUSTED**.
